slides.0.title: Geographical indications: place names on the label
slides.0.subtitle: Decree 283/993 and Law 17.011
slides.1.title: Chapter IV of Decree 283/993
slides.1.highlights.0.title: A certificate is required
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Article 15: a label naming a geographical indication, region of origin or appellation of origin needs a certificate from the competent body proving the right to use it
slides.1.highlights.1.title: INAVI's register
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Article 16: INAVI keeps a Register of Geographical Indications of Origin for qualifying growers and wineries; foreign names on imported wine are registered through their agents
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The grapes must come from there
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Article 17: a geographical indication may be used only if the grapes were grown in that area; INAVI may add measures based on OIV rules
slides.1.content: A place name is not free to use: it needs registration, a certificate and local grapes.
slides.2.title: Law 17.011 of 1998
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Three kinds of name
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A geographical indication: quality or reputation mainly due to origin. An indication of provenance: it only states where something is from and is protected without registration. An appellation of origin: characteristics due exclusively or essentially to the geographical environment, natural and human factors included
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Two registers
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Article 76: the industrial property office keeps registers of geographical indications and appellations, without prejudice to INAVI's register for national producers. Article 77: for national wine, the competent body is INAVI
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The ten-year clause
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Article 79: a geographical name for wine or spirits used continuously for at least ten years before 15 April 1994 is exempt from the general ban. Articles 73–79 were amended by Law 19.670 in 2018
slides.2.content: Law 17.011 is a trademark law, but it hands place names for national wine to INAVI.
slides.3.title: No European-style tiers
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Regions are for describing
slides.3.highlights.0.content: INAVI's website describes the country in several wine regions, but this course found no rule that draws their boundaries or sets grapes or yields for them
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Registration and certificates
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Putting a place on a label depends on INAVI registration and certification, not on a tiered system such as AOC or DOC
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Not verified
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Which names are registered, and when, could not be checked against an official list, so this is not tested
slides.3.content: Remember the order: certificate, register, origin of the grapes.
